per_wilaya_files.rule: each file holds this file's features whose wilaya_code is that code, in this file's order, with the same properties and coordinates
per_wilaya_files.generated: written from this file by scripts/build-commune-boundaries.mjs in the same run and checked byte for byte; never edited on its own

title_fr: Algérie: polygones des limites de commune (1,541)

properties.name_fr: commune name in French, copied from the commune record
properties.name_ar: commune name in Arabic, copied from the commune record
properties.wilaya_code: parent wilaya code as an integer 1-69 (join key to wilayas.json)
properties.wilaya_code_58: the wilaya (1-58) on the 58-wilaya map of Law 19-12, copied from the commune record (see wilaya-lineage.json)
properties.wilaya_code_48: the wilaya (1-48) on the 48-wilaya map of Law 84-09 as it stood just before Law 19-12, copied from the commune record (see wilaya-lineage.json)
properties.postal_code: commune postal code, null for the 1 commune with no citable code
properties.code_commune: commune code as an integer (join key to the commune records, unique)

origin.A: OpenStreetMap admin_level=8 outline from research/_commune-centres/commune-boundaries.json, matched by osm_relation_id
origin.B: geoBoundaries ADM3 polygon, attached only when all five Rule B clauses held (research/_commune-centres/commune-boundary-fills.json)
origin.C: as A, for a commune whose point lies outside its own outline; shipped only because an independent geoBoundaries polygon corroborates it. The point is unchanged.
origin.E: derived: the gap the neighbours and the wilaya outline leave, for a commune that is the only one in its wilaya without an outline, shipped only because an independent geoBoundaries polygon of the same commune overlaps it at shape IoU >= 0.9 (research/_commune-centres/commune-boundary-fills.json). The commune point is not moved even where it falls outside; see derived_outlines.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap: commune boundaries (relation, boundary=administrative, admin_level=8) in Algeria, full geometry

simplification.method: Outlines taken from the committed cache (Douglas-Peucker 0.0005 degrees) and rounded to 4 decimals; Rule B polygons reduced from full resolution with Douglas-Peucker at 0.0005 degrees and rounded to 4 decimals. Exterior rings counter-clockwise.

provenance_notes: Identity comes from the commune records, never from a name: each feature is attached to its code_commune through the OSM relation id the record carries, or through the five-clause Rule B. Properties are copied from the records, not from any source file.
No commune point was read to be changed. The 16 communes in research/_commune-centres/containment-exceptions.json keep the point they have; their outlines ship under Rule C.

Licence: ODbL-1.0 is recorded, while the package itself declares SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE for its mixed terms, because the outlines are OpenStreetMap-derived; the package LICENSE and NOTICE list this file as an ODbL 1.0 part, (c) OpenStreetMap contributors. The geoBoundaries ADM3 file (OSM extract of 2023-01-19, geoBoundaries build of 2023-12-12, boundaryID DZA-ADM3-69997007) supplies the Rule B outlines and the Rule C corroboration; its stated source is OpenStreetMap via osm-boundaries.com, so its outlines carry the same ODbL terms, and NOTICE credits geoBoundaries for them.

repaired_rings lists every ring that touched itself after the cache's simplification or the 4-decimal rounding and was made simple by deleting 1 to 4 vertices; none changed its area by more than 0.03%.
No commune point was moved for a derived outline either: where the point falls outside it, derived_outlines says so.
Absent communes are listed in missing_codes with the reason. No outline was drawn to fill them.
